rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid-range temperature to capture all 10 compounds without truncation and map the overall elution window. This gives initial information on early unretained peaks, late hold elution, and whether temperature or slope changes are likely to matter next.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only available gain is reducing t_last below 10 min. The first run shows all peaks elute well within the gradient and the latest peak corresponds to only about 0.38 organic, so a narrower, steeper window with higher temperature should compress the chromatogram substantially while still keeping all compounds in the gradient.

The same critical pair (6,7) collapsed when the gradient was made much steeper, so test whether that pair is slope-responsive by lengthening tG while keeping the compressed phi window and temperature fixed. This should recover resolution for that pair with only a modest time penalty and will show whether the current optimum is near this region.

The critical pair did not improve with a longer gradient at 50 C, suggesting it is not slope-responsive and instead needs a temperature/selectivity change. Dropping back to 40 C while keeping the fast, narrow gradient should test whether the pair re-separates enough to preserve the near-10 min runtime.

Injection 4 is fully resolved and only slightly too slow, so the next move is a small increase in gradient strength to pull the last peak under 10 min while preserving the successful 40 C selectivity. Raising phi1 one step should shorten the late part of the run with less risk to the critical 6/7 pair than changing temperature again.

We are very close to the maximum: the only deficit is the 6/7 pair at R 1.39 while t_last is already under 10 min. A small increase in tG should selectively recover enough resolution for that pair with only a modest risk of pushing the last peak just over 10 min.

The 6/7 pair needs a small selectivity boost, and lowering temperature helped strongly before, while increasing tG cost too much time. Dropping from 40 to 35 C at the current near-optimal gradient is the best chance to push that pair above R 1.5 while keeping t_last close enough to 10 min for a higher overall CRF.

The best method is already nearly ideal, so now probe whether a slightly shorter, weaker gradient can keep the 6/7 pair at or above 1.5 while shaving more time. Compared with the successful 0.05–0.60, 10 min, 40 C run, shortening tG may bring t_last under 10 min; if resolution stays acceptable this could beat the current best.

Test whether the stronger upper endpoint that nearly optimized CRF at 10 min can be combined with a shorter 8 min gradient to cut time while preserving enough resolution. This directly brackets the current best against the fast 0.60 endpoint method and may reveal a better time/resolution tradeoff near the optimum.

The optimum appears near 10 min at 40 C, with the 6/7 pair just under full credit when phi1 is 0.65. Increasing phi1 one more step may nudge the critical selectivity/window enough to separate 6/7 while still keeping the last peak comfortably under 10 min, offering a chance at CRF 1.000.

The first peak is still fairly early, so raising phi0 one step may trim the unused low-organic region and shift the elution window to improve the crowded midsection without sacrificing the sub-10 min last peak. This tests whether the 6/7 pair responds more to the phi window placement than to gradient steepness alone.

Now that we have a perfect score, the only useful exploration is to see whether the same phi window can be shortened further while retaining full resolution. Reducing tG to 8 min directly tests if injection 11 is robust enough to support an even faster method; if not, we already have the optimum in hand.

With a perfect CRF already achieved, the remaining question is whether a higher temperature can further shorten the run while preserving the now-successful selectivity from the shifted phi window. This is a focused robustness/optimization check around the optimum; if resolution collapses, injection 11 remains the clear best.

The perfect method suggests the key was raising phi0, not pushing phi1 high; lowering phi1 one step may keep the favorable selectivity while potentially improving the critical 6/7 spacing. This tests whether the optimum window can be tightened on the high end without losing the sub-10 min last peak.

Since raising phi0 to 0.10 produced the perfect method, one more step tests whether additional trimming of the low-organic region can further compress the run while preserving the now-adequate critical pair. This is the most plausible remaining way to retain full resolution and still stay under 10 min.

Injection 15 improved the perfect method further in practical speed while keeping all pairs above 1.5, so one more increase in phi0 tests the limit of trimming the low-organic region. If resolution holds, this would be an even faster fully resolved optimum; if not, injection 15 is the better operating point.

Injection 15 is perfect and injection 16 suggests we are near the phi0 limit, so keep the stronger successful phi0=0.15 and test whether a slightly higher phi1 can shorten the late tail without hurting the critical 6/7 pair. This explores the remaining nearby window around the current best fully resolved method.

The remaining untested neighbor around the perfect region is to keep the successful phi0=0.15 but lower phi1 one step, which may widen the critical mid-gradient spacing while still staying under the 10 min target. This checks whether the best practical operating point is a slightly tighter upper window than injection 15.

A higher temperature alone hurt the 6/7 pair, but combining it with a slightly longer gradient may restore resolution while potentially keeping the last peak under 10 min. This is a final nearby check of whether time can be traded for selectivity differently than at 40 C around the perfect window.

The remaining unexplored local axis around the perfect window is lower temperature, which could increase selectivity for the critical 6/7 pair while likely still keeping the last peak under 10 min given the strong phi window. This is a final robustness check near the best method; if it slows too much, the 40 C perfect methods remain preferred.

With several perfect methods already found, use the remaining budget to define robustness on the slope axis around the practical favorite at phi0 0.15, phi1 0.65, 40 C. A slightly longer gradient should confirm how much margin the critical 6/7 pair has without changing the successful selectivity pattern.

The remaining nearby untested corner is a tighter window on both ends, which may keep the shortened runtime of high phi0 while recovering some of the 6/7 spacing lost at phi0 0.20, phi1 0.65. This is a sensible final local map point around the best fully resolved region.

The trend from phi0 0.10 to 0.20 suggests higher phi0 can keep resolution acceptable while accelerating the run, and tightening phi1 to 0.60 preserved full resolution at phi0 0.20. One more step to phi0 0.25 probes the true upper limit of low-end trimming near the optimum region.

Phi0 0.25 is too high because the first two peaks are compressing near the dead-time region, so back off to phi0 0.20 and tighten phi1 one step lower to see if the late peak can be pulled just under 10 min while maintaining full resolution. This is one of the last sensible local refinements around the best high-phi0 methods.

For the final shot, combine the fast high-phi0 setting that nearly stayed fully resolved at 10 min with a shorter gradient to test whether the last peak can be accelerated further without sacrificing too much on the critical pair. We already have CRF 1.000 secured, so this is a last boundary probe around the fastest promising fully resolved region.
